Question 1

Consider the linear transformation T with matrix representation T, given by T=[−1−1−11].

The triangle △ABC is shown above. Which of the following is △A′B′C′, the image of △ABC under the action of T?

a
b
c
d
e
Submit

decision.explanation: T(x,y)=(-x-y,-x+y). Thus A(2,1) maps to A′(-3,-1), B(2,2) maps to B′(-4,0), and C(0,2) maps to C′(-2,2). These vertices match option d.

after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14073357/assets/7bfcc5c729475256b70211bcf18e94b605e4486790b13794eaa46cce4f6461bb.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown above. Which of the following is $△{A}^{′}{B}^{′}{C}^{′},$ the image of $△ABC$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
To find the image of $T$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $△ABC:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $△{A}^{′}{B}^{′}{C}^{′}$ are $(-3,-1),(-4,0),(-2,2)$, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14073357/assets/548c907226db9cbdc8fb4dd18c74f3a2001ba7d90973c6f433f67b3e6b87fd29.png)

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(-1,2)$ and $B(1,1).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(0,5)$ and ${B}^{′}(3,1).$

To find the image of AB― under the action of T, we first create a matrix X containing the coordinates of the endpoints of AB―:

content.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(-1,2)$ and $B(1,1).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(0,5)$ and ${B}^{′}(3,1).$
